question: Which state became the first to implement "New Education Policy" at pre-primary level?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uttarakhand became the first state to implement the New Education Policy at the pre-primary level.**
 
• **The New Education Policy (NEP) was approved by the Union Cabinet in July 2020.**
 
• It aims to bring transformational changes in the **education system** and make it more** holistic, flexible, and multidisciplinary.**
 
• The NEP emphasizes the need to focus on early childhood care and education (ECCE) and lays down guidelines for the same.
 
• It recommends that children between the ages of 3 and 6 should have access to free and compulsory ECCE.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uttarakhand's **move to implement the NEP at the** pre-primary level** is a significant step towards achieving the policy's goals.
 
• **The state has already started training its teachers and preparing the curriculum for the new system.**
 
• **Tamil Nadu, Haryana, and Kerala are also among the states that have shown interest in implementing the NEP.**
 
• However, they are yet to make any** official announcements** regarding the same.
